title: A whole-brain Drosophila connectome model predicts a duration- and sign-dependent potassium trap after anoxia and a reset-based route to functional recovery
author: Srihari Muralikrishnan, Kalaris Labs (http://kalarislabs.com/), ORCID 0009-0004-0220-0361, GitHub @sriharideveloper
ai_disclosure: AI system Claude (Anthropic) assisted under the author's direction (not an author); Aryan Kumar Jha (Kalaris Labs) credited for AI (Claude) work; Kalaris Labs skills Myriad and Research Agent Skills used.
usage_rule: Downstream messaging must use only these claims, with their numbers and confidence qualifiers; always include K15. Paths are relative to D:\FRUITFLY.

claims.claim: Headline: in a connectome-constrained LIF model with a phenomenological K+/ATP layer, abrupt reoxygenation can trap the model brain in a self-sustained K+-coupled high-activity state; a 10-20 s total activity block releases it. The trap is robust after long (180 s) anoxia and sign-sensitive after short (30 s) anoxia.
claims.number: 180 s: runaway in 48/48 parameter sets (FAFB) and 5/5 MCNS runs; 30 s with antennal-lobe local neurons inhibitory: 0/3 FAFB runaway
claims.confidence: high (180 s); moderate (30 s sign sensitivity)

claims.claim: Under the default transmitter-sign rule, naive (abrupt) reoxygenation produced the runaway after as little as 7 s of anoxia at 22 C in the FAFB model.
claims.number: 30/30 runs from 7 to 480 s anoxia; FII_norm ~0; late firing 105-119 Hz/neuron
claims.confidence: high for default signs; NOT valid under corrected antennal-lobe signs (see K03) - do not use '7 s' without this qualifier

claims.claim: Setting antennal-lobe local neurons inhibitory (147 sign changes in FAFB, 219 in MCNS) removed the high-rate runaway and the identity loss after 30 s anoxia. MCNS and FAFB-proxy kept a weak low-rate oscillation that the preregistered classifier still counts as runaway.
claims.number: FAFB variant A 0/3 runaway (late 0.035-0.17 Hz/neuron, raw FII 0.915-0.936); MCNS FII_norm 1.000 [0.996, 1.002] (3.0 Hz/neuron residual), delta +0.949 [+0.918, +0.977]; FAFB-proxy 0.859 (0.82 Hz/neuron)
claims.confidence: moderate (n = 3 FAFB, n = 5 MCNS/proxy; variants B, C not run)

claims.claim: After 180 s anoxia the runaway persisted with corrected antennal-lobe signs, and the 20-s total block still rescued identity.
claims.number: MCNS naive FII_norm -0.135 (FSA 0.897) vs block 0.989; FAFB-proxy naive -0.125 vs block 0.965

claims.claim: A 20-s total activity block at reperfusion restored the stimulus-response map; 2-5 s blocks failed; the block worked even when started 20 s late.
claims.number: FAFB FII_norm 1.001 / 0.953 at 30 / 180 s anoxia; rescue in 48/48 parameter sets at 30 s, 34/48 (0.71 [0.58, 0.83]) at 180 s

claims.claim: Releasing the block as soon as K+ and ATP had normalised was not enough: the network re-ignited.
claims.number: closed-loop criterion met after 11 s; MCNS runaway 5/5 (11.3 Hz/neuron), delta vs 20-s block -0.071 [-0.081, -0.058]; FAFB-proxy delta -0.674 [-0.742, -0.624]
claims.confidence: moderate (MCNS + proxy only, 180 s, default signs)

claims.claim: The maintained runaway is ionic, not synaptic: it survives removal of all synapses and collapses when activity-dependent K+ accumulation is removed; quiet and active states coexist in the intact network.
claims.number: all synapses off: 109/134 Hz/neuron; K+ clamp 5 mM: 2.4/2.3 Hz/neuron; hysteresis >= 13 mV

claims.claim: Simulated 'brain death' (silent and unresponsive) occurred only with near-total neuron death; the model never produced a silent but structurally intact brain.
claims.number: 92 runs, all with >= 97.9% of neurons dead (of 1,209 FAFB runs)

claims.claim: After the reset, remaining identity loss was due to neuron death; protecting the top 1% most-connected neurons was far more efficient per neuron than whole-brain protection, in two connectomes.
Cooling before/during the insult widened the recoverable window, but the size of the effect is set by the model's injury rule; cooling only during reperfusion was harmful.
claims.confidence: high that it holds; magnitude is by construction, not a prediction

claims.claim: Graded (ramped or pulsed) reperfusion did not beat abrupt reperfusion plus a block (preregistered H3 falsified, direction reversed).
claims.number: 360 s: ramp30 delta FII_norm -0.331 [-0.583, -0.130]; ramp60 +6.6 pp dead
claims.confidence: high within model (no oxidative/inflammatory mechanisms modelled)

claims.claim: Structurally, random neuron loss degrades sensorimotor reachability gradually (no sharp threshold), whereas hub- or demand-targeted loss is far more destructive, in all four connectomes.
claims.number: FAFB random f_c 0.800 (width 0.671); area-weighted 0.277 (ratio 0.346); hub 0.033 (ratio 0.041); direction replicates 4/4
claims.confidence: high (direction); magnitudes differ across datasets (f_c max/min up to 23.35)

claims.claim: Wiring statistics predict how much identity returns after the reset, but not whether the network gets trapped.
claims.number: post-reset FII: cross-validated R2 0.964 [0.940, 0.978] (excitatory core size); runaway among viable networks: AUC 0.53 (chance)
claims.confidence: moderate (FAFB only, 1,118 of 1,209 runs, default signs, no standalone report)

claims.claim: The small 'driver core' (0.5% of neurons) that rescued after 30 s anoxia under default signs is not established: it is centred on the antennal-lobe neurons whose sign correction removes the 30-s runaway.
claims.number: 279 of 696 driver neurons in the antennal lobes; after 180 s, 20% of the brain had to be blocked
claims.confidence: low (likely sign artefact) - do not message as a finding

claims.claim: Scope: all results are predictions of a simplified simulation (connectome-constrained LIF + phenomenological metabolism, constants not fitted to Drosophila). They are not evidence about living tissue, clinical brain death or human resuscitation; resuscitation of a brain-dead organism has not been demonstrated.
claims.number: 3,487 analysed simulated condition-seed runs; dynamics in 2 connectomes (FAFB, MCNS); BANC dynamics not analysed
